previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with palpitations and worsening shortness of breath following a recent hospitalization for multifocal pneumonia and COPD exacerbation. He was found to have atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, decompensated systolic heart failure, and signs of recurrent pulmonary infiltrate. Treatment included rate control with metoprolol, diuresis for fluid overload, and completion of antibiotic therapy. His COPD was managed with steroids and bronchodilators, and he was transitioned from Advair to fluticasone to reduce cardiac stimulation. His kidney function improved with hydration. He received methadone for opioid withdrawal and expressed strong motivation to pursue recovery. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for cardiology, pulmonary, and addiction services.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with diaphoresis.  Evaluation for acute process.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to radiographs of the chest from ___.

FINDINGS:

PA and lateral views of the chest demonstrate interval resolution of right
lung base opacity since the prior study.  There remains a small amount of
atelectasis in the left lung base.  Otherwise, the lungs are clear with no
sign of pleural effusion, pulmonary edema, pneumothorax or focal consolidation
concerning for pneumonia.  The heart size is mildly enlarged, as before.  The
mediastinal contours are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary process.  Interval resolution of right lung base
opacity since the prior study.

HISTORY:  ___ male with positive D-dimer and left lower quadrant pain.
Evaluation for pulmonary embolism chest and acute pathology in the abdomen or
pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained through the thorax after
the dynamic administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque intravenous contrast. 
Reformatted coronal, sagittal and oblique maximum intensity projection images
were reviewed.  Subsequently, portal venous phase images were obtained of the
abdomen and pelvis.  Images were presented in the axial, coronal and sagittal
planes.

DLP:  1805.01 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to CT of the thorax from ___ and
CT of the abdomen and pelvis from the ___.

FINDINGS:

CTA THORAX:  The aorta and its major branch vessels are well opacified.  There
is no evidence of dissection, intramural hematoma, focal stenosis, occlusion
or aneurysmal formation.  The pulmonary arteries are well opacified to the
subsegmental level.  There is no evidence of filling defect within the main,
right, left, lobar, segmental or subsegmental pulmonary arteries.  The heart
is mildly enlarged, as before.  There are dense atherosclerotic calcifications
are present within the coronary vessels.  There is no pericardial or pleural
effusion.  The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There is no supraclavicular,
mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymph node enlargement by CT size criteria.

Persistent ground-glass opacities in the bilateral upper lobes are again seen,
compatible with residual multifocal pneumonia, as described previously but
somewhat improved.  There has been interval increase in opacity in the
lingula.  The previously seen right pleural effusion has resolved.

CT ABDOMEN:  The liver enhances homogeneously, with no evidence of focal
lesions.  There is no intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. 
The gallbladder is decompressed.  The pancreas, spleen, and bilateral adrenal
glands are normal in appearance.  A 1.7 cm simple cyst in the lower pole of
the right kidney is unchanged (2b:134).  A small right interpolar calyceal
diverticulum (2b:119) is unchanged.  Otherwise, the kidneys present symmetric
nephrograms excretion of contrast.  There is no evidence of hydronephrosis or
perinephric abnormality.  

The stomach is distended with ingested material, but otherwise unremarkable. 
The duodenum and intra-abdominal loops of small bowel are unremarkable, with
no evidence of wall thickening or obstruction.  The intra-abdominal loops of
large bowel contains a moderate amount of stool throughout, but are otherwise
unremarkable with no evidence of wall thickening or surrounding fat stranding.
The appendix is not visualized, but there are no secondary inflammatory signs
to suggest appendicitis.  No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy is
noted by CT size criteria.  There is no intra-abdominal free air or free
fluid.  Atrophy of the right rectus abdominus is again seen.  Diffuse
subcutaneous soft tissue of the edema along the abdominal wall is unchanged
since the prior study.

CT PELVIS:  The urinary bladder and terminal ureters are unremarkable.  There
is no pelvic free fluid.  The rectum and sigmoid colon are unremarkable. 
There is no pelvic sidewall or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  No abdominal wall or
inguinal hernias are present. 

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No lytic or blastic lesions suspicious for malignancy is
present.

IMPRESSION:

1. No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic pathology.

2. Residual ground-glass opacities in the bilateral upper lobes have improved
but are slightly worse in the lingula, and may represent multifocal pneumonia,
as described on the prior CT from ___.  Interval resolution of small
right pleural effusion.

3. No acute pathology in the abdomen or pelvis.
